title: How Capital Gains Taxes Work When You Sell a Home
bigPicture: Most seniors can sell their home and not pay capital gains tax on the profit.
whatYouNeedToKnow: You usually don't owe tax on the first $250,000 of profit if you're single, or $500,000 if you're married.
To get this break, you must have lived in the home for at least 2 out of the last 5 years.
Any profit above those amounts is what you'll pay tax on.
commonMistakesToAvoid: Assuming you owe tax on every dollar of profit, even if you lived there a long time.
Forgetting to count home improvement costs, which can lower your taxable profit.
actionSteps: Calculate your total profit by subtracting what you paid from what you sold it for.
Check if you lived in the home for 2 out of the last 5 years to see if you qualify for the tax-free break.
